title: Scaling Discovery through Test-Time Communication
abstract: Science advances not in isolation but through collaboration, yet existing agentic systems capture little of this. Whether communicating agents help remains an open question with mixed prior results. We show that test-time communication can substantially outperform independent parallel attempts on challenging tasks, where sharing a breakthrough can push the whole group forward. We first study the effect of scaling multi-agent test-time communication, where agents have no predefined roles and communicate via a shared directory, on ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark requiring novel problem solving. We find that a team of $k$ communicating agents, team@$k$, matches the success rate of $4k$ independent agents, and this advantage grows with $k$, suggesting gains compound with scale. The effect is not merely efficiency: a task that no single agent can solve, a team of agents can solve reliably. Furthermore, these gains transfer to research-oriented tasks, given sufficient compute. On polyomino packing, communicating agents outperform best@$k$ and exceed the prior best-known score. On MNIST classifier compression, communication surpasses the best-known human solution. A team of four agents produced a 1,957-byte classifier submission achieving 99.4% test accuracy, smaller than both the best-known human solution and the best single-agent result. These gains are not unconditional. Independent agents may outperform communication when compute is limited or when a clear measure of progress is absent. However, under sufficient compute and clear feedback, multi-agent communication consistently yields stronger results.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Welcome to Advanced Topics in Multi-Agent Systems. Today's lecture is on “Scaling Discovery through Test-Time Communication,” a paper from researchers at UC Berkeley and Microsoft Research. We've seen a lot of work recently in this space, like “AutoScientists” and “AgentRxiv,” which focus on building collaborative frameworks for agents. This paper takes a slightly different angle, focusing specifically on how unstructured, peer-to-peer communication during inference time can improve problem-solving, rather than relying on a central coordinator or explicit task decomposition. It's a key question as we try to scale agent capabilities. Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 欢迎来到多智能体系统进阶专题。今天这节课讲的是《通过测试时通信扩展发现能力》，这篇论文来自加州大学伯克利分校和微软研究院的研究人员。最近这个领域出了不少工作，比如“AutoScientists”和“AgentRxiv”，它们主要关注为智能体搭建协作框架。而这篇论文的角度稍有不同，它专门研究在推理阶段，非结构化的、点对点的通信如何提升问题解决能力，而不是依赖一个中心协调者或者显式的任务分解。在我们试图扩展智能体能力的过程中，这是一个关键问题。好，诺亚？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Excuse me, Professor. You mentioned it differs from task decomposition. So if the agents aren't being assigned sub-problems, how do they actually collaborate instead of just running in parallel?
segments.zh: 不好意思，教授。您提到它和任务分解不一样。那如果智能体并没有被分配子问题，它们到底是怎么协作的，而不是只是并行运行呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's the central question the paper addresses. The core concept is what they call 'verified progress sharing.' Instead of having ten agents independently trying to solve a problem from start to finish, this approach has them work on the same problem in a shared environment. When one agent makes a verifiable improvement—say, it writes a piece of code that scores higher on a test—it shares that progress. Another agent can then pick up that improved code and build on it. The main comparison they make is between a communicating team of 'k' agents, which they call 'team at k', and the best result from 'k' independent agents, or 'best at k'.
segments.zh: 这正是论文要回答的核心问题。核心概念是他们所说的“可验证进展共享”。不是让十个智能体各自独立地从头到尾解决问题，而是让它们在共享环境中处理同一个问题。当一个智能体取得了可验证的改进——比如它写了一段代码，在测试中得分更高——它就会共享这个进展。另一个智能体就可以接着拿这段改进后的代码继续往下做。他们做的主要对比是：一个由“k”个智能体组成的、能互相通信的团队，他们称之为“team at k”，对比“k”个独立智能体中的最佳结果，也就是“best at k”。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the hypothesis is that a team can combine breakthroughs more efficiently than any single agent can discover them all sequentially?
segments.zh: 所以这个假设就是，团队能把各自的突破组合起来，效率比任何单个智能体从头到尾依次发现所有突破都要高？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Precisely. Think of it like a relay race versus a set of individual sprints. In independent sampling, or 'best at k', you're betting that one of your sprinters is fast enough to win the whole race alone. With 'team at k', you're letting the fastest agent for each leg of the race hand off the baton. If a problem requires ten sequential discoveries, independent agents each have to make all ten discoveries on their own. The communicating team can, in theory, combine the single fastest discovery for each of the ten steps, even if those discoveries come from ten different agents. This allows for a cumulative search process, rather than a purely parallel one.
segments.zh: 正是如此。你可以把它想象成接力赛和各自跑百米冲刺的区别。在独立采样，也就是“best at k”里，你赌的是你某一个短跑选手足够快，能一个人赢下整场比赛。而在“team at k”里，你是让每一棒最快的智能体去交接接力棒。如果一个任务需要十步连续的发现，独立智能体每一个都得自己完成全部十步。而互相通信的团队，理论上可以把这十步里每一步最快的那个发现组合起来，哪怕这些发现来自十个不同的智能体。这就实现了一个累积式的搜索过程，而不是纯粹的并行搜索。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: That makes sense in theory, but how does that work in practice? Is there a risk of them all converging on the same mediocre idea too early?
segments.zh: 理论上说得通，但实际中怎么运作呢？会不会有风险，大家太早就收敛到同一个平庸的想法上？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: A very real risk, and the methodology tries to account for that. The communication protocol is surprisingly simple. There's no central orchestrator. The agents, which are identical, communicate through a shared digital workspace. This includes an append-only log for findings, a log for failed ideas, and a shared artifact, like a codebase, that they can all edit. To prevent premature convergence, agents are explicitly instructed to select different initial approaches and to only adopt another agent's work after observing a measured, objective improvement. Even then, they're told to try and maintain some variation. The key is the 'verified' part of progress sharing—it relies on tasks where you can get a reliable score for partial solutions.
segments.zh: 确实存在这个风险，而他们的方法也试图解决这个问题。通信协议出奇地简单。没有中央协调器。所有智能体都是相同的，它们通过一个共享的数字工作空间来交流。这个空间包括一个只追加的发现日志、一个失败想法的日志，以及一个共享的产物，比如一个代码库，所有人都可以编辑。为了防止过早收敛，智能体被明确指示选择不同的初始方法，并且只有在观察到可衡量的、客观的改进之后，才会采纳另一个智能体的工作。即便如此，它们也被要求尽量保持一定的多样性。关键在于进展共享中“已验证”这部分——它依赖于那些能对部分解决方案给出可靠评分的任务。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: What kinds of tasks did they use? That verification requirement seems like it would be hard to satisfy for many real-world problems.
segments.zh: 他们用了哪些任务？这个验证要求，对很多现实世界的问题来说似乎很难满足。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: You've hit on a critical point. The tasks were chosen specifically because they have clear, intermediate scoring mechanisms. First, they used ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark of interactive grid-world games where progress is measured by levels cleared. Second, they used a polyomino packing problem, which is an algorithmic task where a submitted program gets a continuous packing score. The third was an MNIST classifier compression task, where the goal is to minimize file size while maintaining high accuracy. In all these cases, an agent can test a new idea and get immediate, objective feedback on whether it's an improvement. The results were quite telling. For instance, on the ARC games, a team of 5 agents performed as well as 33 independent agents, a more than six-fold efficiency gain.
segments.zh: 你点到了一个关键问题。这些任务之所以被选中，正是因为它们有清晰、可量化的中间评分机制。第一，他们用了ARC-AGI-3，这是一个交互式网格世界游戏的基准，进度通过通关层数来衡量。第二，他们用了一个多联骨牌拼装问题，这是一个算法任务，提交的程序会得到一个连续的拼装得分。第三是MNIST分类器压缩任务，目标是在保持高准确率的同时最小化文件大小。在所有这些情况下，智能体都能测试一个新想法，并立即获得客观反馈，判断它是否有所改进。结果很能说明问题。比如在ARC游戏上，5个智能体组成的团队表现得和33个独立智能体一样好，效率提升超过六倍。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: That's a significant multiplier. In the polyomino packing and MNIST tasks, did they just find solutions faster, or did they find qualitatively different or better solutions?
segments.zh: 这可是一笔可观的效率倍增。在polyomino拼图和MNIST任务上，它们只是更快找到了解法，还是找到了性质不同或更好的解法？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: They found better solutions that independent agents couldn't reach. In the polyomino task, the team surpassed the previous best-known result after independent agents had already plateaued. Trace analysis showed one agent would invent a concept, another would implement it more efficiently, and a third would add a complementary heuristic on top. Similarly, for MNIST compression, the team produced a final classifier that was about 20% smaller than a human reference solution by combining several distinct techniques discovered by different agents during the run, including one from a branch that was no longer the individual leader.
segments.zh: 他们找到了独立智能体无法达到的更好解决方案。在polyomino任务中，团队在独立智能体已经停滞之后，超越了此前已知的最佳结果。轨迹分析显示，一个智能体会发明一个概念，另一个会更高效地实现它，第三个则会在其上叠加一个互补的启发式方法。同样，在MNIST压缩任务中，团队通过结合不同智能体在运行过程中发现的几种不同技术，包括来自一个已不再是单独领先者的分支的技术，最终产出的分类器比人类参考解决方案小了约20%。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The significance here is that communication can change the scaling dynamics of test-time compute. It suggests that for complex, open-ended problems common in science and engineering, the path forward might not just be more independent shots on goal, but smarter collaboration. This shifts the focus toward designing agent systems with reliable intermediate verifiers. However, the paper is also clear about the limitations. The authors ran an experiment on Terminal-Bench 2.0, where feedback is often delayed or ambiguous.
segments.zh: 这里的重要意义在于，沟通可以改变测试时计算的扩展动态。它表明，对于科学和工程中常见的复杂、开放式问题，前进的道路可能不只是更多独立的尝试，而是更聪明的协作。这就把焦点转向了设计带有可靠中间验证器的智能体系统。不过，这篇论文也很清楚地指出了局限性。作者在 Terminal-Bench 2.0 上做了一个实验，那里的反馈往往是延迟的或模糊的。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: And what happened there? Did communication hurt performance?
segments.zh: 那结果怎么样？沟通反而拖累了表现吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It performed worse than two independent attempts. The takeaway is that without a clear, objective signal of progress, agents can get stuck reinforcing each other's mistakes or converging on a flawed solution. This aligns with findings from other work like CooperBench, which also shows that collaboration can fail without the right conditions. This paper's contribution is in isolating one of those key conditions: the ability to verify progress. When that condition is met, communication can be remarkably effective.
segments.zh: 它的表现还不如两次独立尝试。结论就是，如果没有一个清晰、客观的进展信号，智能体可能会陷在互相强化彼此错误的状态里，或者一起收敛到一个有缺陷的方案上。这和CooperBench等其他工作的发现是一致的，它们同样表明，缺乏合适条件时协作是会失败的。这篇论文的贡献在于分离出了其中一个关键条件：验证进展的能力。当这个条件满足时，沟通可以变得非常有效。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: So, to wrap up, this work provides strong evidence for a conditional claim. It's not saying communication is always better. It's saying that when agents have enough compute and a reliable way to measure partial progress, a team can solve problems that are out of reach for individual agents working alone. The key takeaway is that effective collaboration isn't just about talking; it's about sharing verifiable success. This insight helps steer the design of future multi-agent systems toward creating environments with clear feedback loops. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 总之，总结一下，这项工作为一个有条件的论断提供了有力证据。它并不是说沟通总是更好，而是说当智能体拥有足够的算力，并且有可靠的方法来衡量阶段性进展时，团队就能解决单个智能体独自无法企及的问题。关键结论是，有效的协作不只是靠交流，更在于共享可验证的成功。这一洞见有助于引导未来多智能体系统的设计，朝着构建具有清晰反馈回路的环境方向发展。感谢收听。如果还有任何问题，可以询问我们的AI助手，或者留言评论。
